kinds.d: Dye made for colouring fabric and fibre, from cold-water fibre-reactive to hot-water household dye.

x.d: Cold-water fibre-reactive dye that permanently dyes cellulose fibres at room temperature; also dyes wool and silk with acid.
x.dt: cotton, linen, viscose, hemp · intermixable colours

x.d: American household dye first sold in 1916, in powder and solid forms, applied in hot water.
British dye brand founded 1946; Machine Fabric Dye in 32 colours, Hand Dye in 21, Multipurpose in 26.

kinds.d: Plant, insect or mineral dyes and indigo, used in vats for resist and shibori work.

x.d: Indigo is insoluble and must be reduced to its soluble form in a vat; air then turns the dyed cloth blue. Japan used a heated vat of anaerobic bacteria.
x.dt: Indigofera, Persicaria or Strobilanthes · fermentation or chemical reduction

kinds.d: Hot wax and its pen-like copper applicator used to draw dye-resist designs on cloth.

x.d: Pen-like tool with a copper wax reservoir, spout and bamboo handle that applies hot wax in Javanese batik tulis, possibly from the 12th century.
x.dt: copper, bronze, zinc, iron or Teflon · one to seven spouts

kinds.d: Paint made to decorate fabric, heat-set or air-cured.

x.d: Water-based acrylic fluid textile paint with the consistency of water, for washes, silk painting and airbrushing.
x.dt: heat-set with a dry iron · dry-cleanable

x.d: 45 ml textile paints in Opaque, Light Fabric and Shimmer types.

brands.d: US maker of Dye-Na-Flow fluid textile paint.
French maker of Setacolor textile paints.
American household dye brand owned by Nakoma Products.
British dye brand now owned by Henkel.
US craft brand of dimensional fabric paint.

traditions.d: Japanese tie-dye by binding, stitching, folding or clamping cloth before dyeing.
traditions.tech: Kanoko, miura, kumo, nui, arashi and itajime resists before dyeing.
traditions.auth: Some historic techniques, like original tsujigahana, cannot be fully recreated as the fabric is no longer made.

traditions.d: Wax-resist dyeing in which hot wax drawn with a canting or stamped keeps dye from parts of the cloth.
traditions.tech: Wax is applied, cloth dyed, wax removed by scraping or boiling, and the process repeated for each colour.
traditions.mat: Cotton or silk; wax (malam); copper canting
traditions.auth: Hand-drawn batik shows wax lines on both sides of the cloth.

traditions.p: documented to the 1930s and revived from the 1960s
traditions.d: Yoruba indigo cloth made by women with tied, stitched and paste-resist methods.
traditions.tech: Oniko (tying), alabere (stitching) and eleko (cassava paste); cloth dyed repeatedly, up to 25 or more times.
traditions.auth: Deep blue-black from many dips distinguishes quality cloth.

traditions.d: Indian tie-dye in which tiny points of cloth are tied to leave dotted patterns.
traditions.tech: Cloth is plucked and tied tightly at points, then dyed in stages.
traditions.auth: Bhuj is known for red bandhani.

notes: Aizome and boro: no retrieved page covered them (aizome folded into natural indigo vat; boro left out). Dharma Procion, Jacquard Procion MX: product pages blocked or unretrieved, so Procion MX is a maker-free archetype. Tulip kept as a flat model (no page). Traditions from Wikipedia; Pebeo founding from knowledge.
